definitions.gloss: tidying up; organizing; putting things in order
definitions.explanation: the act of arranging items neatly and systematically, often used as a set phrase emphasizing thorough organization

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}の{整理整頓|せいりせいとん}をする。
{整理整頓|せいりせいとん}が{苦手|にがて}だ。
{仕事|しごと}を{始|はじ}める{前|まえ}に{机|つくえ}の{整理整頓|せいりせいとん}をした。
examples.english: I tidied up my desk before starting work.

notes:
A {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} combining {整理|せいり} (sorting, organizing — deciding what to keep) and {整頓|せいとん} (arranging neatly — putting things in their place). Together they emphasize thorough organization.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {整理整頓|せいりせいとん}する: to organize and tidy up
- {整理整頓|せいりせいとん}が{行|い}き{届|とど}く: to be thoroughly organized
- {整理整頓|せいりせいとん}が{苦手|にがて}: to be bad at organizing

CULTURAL NOTE:
Often seen on signs in schools and workplaces. {整理整頓|せいりせいとん} is considered a fundamental virtue in Japanese culture, taught from elementary school onward.

RELATED:
- {片|かた}づける: to tidy up (casual, everyday)
- {断捨離|だんしゃり}: decluttering (modern concept, minimalism-oriented)
- {整理|せいり}: organizing/sorting (used alone as well)
